hook.text: This is a content studio. It lives in your terminal, and you use it by talking to it.

brand1.text: First run, it asks about your brand. Your colours, your type, the way you sound.

brand2.text: It writes the answers into one file, and from then on, everything you make wears it.

ground.text: Point it at your own sources too — your site, your docs, your app. It reads those instead of guessing, so you are not correcting the same thing every time.

ask.text: Then you just say what you want.

carousel.text: A carousel about the new pricing. It writes the copy, builds the slides, renders the images, and shows you the picture.

iterate.text: Slide two feels flat? Say so. It re-renders in seconds.

print.text: Decks work the same way. However many slides you need, all in your brand.

deckplay.text: And the same slides present themselves. Every one builds as you talk, without anyone animating anything. Send the PDF, or send the film.

essay.text: Writing a long piece? You get the article, the hero image, the share card and the caption, all in one go.

video1.text: Videos too, and this is the fun part.

video2.text: Every frame is just HTML, screenshotted by a browser. The sound is synthesized from a little JSON file.

video3.text: And the motion is one paused timeline. Nothing plays. The renderer asks it for a frame, so the picture can never drift from the voice.

video4.text: There is no video editor anywhere in this. Not even for what you just watched.

calendar.text: Tell it a post went out, and the calendar ticks itself and re-renders the board.

agnostic.text: And it is not tied to one AI. It is just files and a folder of instructions, so point whichever model you already pay for at it.

hour.text: One hour on a Monday gets you a week of content.

close.text: It is open source. Yours in five minutes.
